summary: Describes a framework for composing and aggregating IP Performance Metrics across time and space, so measurements of parts of a path can be combined into a view of the whole. It is the basis for follow-on documents. It is informational.

eli5.summary: If you know how long each part of a trip takes, this explains how to combine those into the time for the whole trip.

questions: what is spatial aggregation of metrics
subtitle: How to combine measurements of parts of a network path, or of short time spans, into an estimate for the whole.

tldr.problem: Measuring every path between every pair of nodes is impossible in a large network, and one set of measurements has to serve both quick troubleshooting and long-term trend views.
tldr.mechanism: The framework defines three kinds of composition (temporal aggregation, spatial aggregation and spatial composition) and sets out what every composed metric definition must state, including how far it may deviate from the true value.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational framework that other documents build on. It covers only packet loss, delay and delay variation, and treats reordering and duplication as research topics.

facts.label: Composition classes
facts.value: Temporal aggregation, spatial aggregation, spatial composition

today: RFC 5835 is an Informational RFC (April 2010) and has not been obsoleted or updated. It remains a framework that metric-specific documents can build on.

sections.title: Why Compose Metrics
sections.content:
The IP Performance Metrics (IPPM) framework in RFC 2330 describes two forms of metric composition, spatial and temporal. This memo expands on them for three classes: temporal aggregation, spatial aggregation and spatial composition.

The RFC gives several motivations. A network's measurement possibilities scale with the square of the number of nodes, so in a large network it is impossible to measure from every node to all others. Operators can instead measure along topology lines and estimate other pairs when needed, accepting some additional error. Where a path crosses several networks, each operator can measure its own part and the complete path can be estimated from the pieces.

Short-term results needed by operations can be combined into longer-term results for capacity planners, and a problem in the measurement system can be isolated to one short measurement. Spatial methods can also produce a single figure of merit for overall network delay, which may be useful in Service Level Agreements.
sections.eli5: You cannot time every possible walk between every pair of houses in a big town. Timing a few short stretches and adding them up is much cheaper, even if the answer is a little less exact.

sections.title: Key Terms
sections.content:
A complete path is the actual path a packet follows from Source to Destination, and may span several networks. A sub-path is a portion of it, and a sub-path metric quantifies the performance of one sub-path.

A composed metric is an estimate of an actual metric for a path over some time interval, derived from other metrics by a deterministic composition function. The ground truth is the actual performance of the path over the interval. It is the complete path metric that the composed metric tries to estimate, and it is generally unavailable.

Adjoining sub-paths join at hosts. If the hosts are co-located and the link between them adds negligible performance, they can be treated as equivalent. If the link between them does contribute, it forms another sub-path that should be included in the composed metric.
sections.eli5: The real answer for the whole trip is the ground truth. The estimate you build from the parts is the composed metric, and the recipe for adding the parts is the composition function.

sections.title: Three Kinds of Composition
sections.content:
Temporal aggregation combines metrics of the same type and scope from different time windows. For example, taking the maximum of 12 consecutive 5-minute maximum one-way delays gives a 60-minute maximum. It reduces stored data and makes cycles and trends easier to see. Higher-order composition can repeat the step: 24 hourly metrics can be aggregated to estimate a day.

Spatial aggregation combines metrics of the same type but different scope to estimate the performance of a larger network, possibly weighting the inputs. The RFC's example weights each origin-destination pair's delay by its share of total load. Publishing a single maximum edge-to-edge delay is another example.

Spatial composition concatenates metrics of the same type over adjacent scopes, so the result represents a direct measurement over the whole sequence. One example is estimating OWD_AC from OWD_AB and OWD_BC. Here all sub-paths contribute equally, independent of traffic load.

Help metrics, such as computing a variance from a sum and a sum of squares, are plain calculations and are not covered. Temporal composition in the RFC 2330 sense, predicting future values from past ones, is also out of scope.
sections.eli5: Adding up many short time slices gives a longer time. Mixing many places gives a town-wide picture. Gluing neighbouring road pieces end to end gives the whole road.

sections.title: What Every Composed Metric Must Say
sections.content:
Definitions of composed metrics MUST include sections covering six topics: the definition and statistic, the composition or aggregation relationship, the conjecture and statistical assumptions behind it, a justification of practical usefulness, examples of how the conjecture could be wrong, and the information to be reported.

Each definition must also state its applicable circumstances: whether it needs the same measurement methodology throughout, and which sending streams (Poisson, Periodic, or both); whether it needs information only available inside one operator's network; how tightly time intervals must be synchronized; whether component metrics must be independent; and what the known sources of error are.

The scope is limited to metrics composed from primary metrics by a deterministic function, and to packet loss, delay and delay variation. Composition of reordering and duplication metrics is considered a research topic. If a component of the process is encumbered by IPR, the composed metric may be too.
sections.eli5: Anyone who invents a new way to add up measurements has to write down the recipe, what they are assuming, when it works, and how it could go wrong.

sections.title: Guidelines: Ground Truth, Gaps and Time Variation
sections.content:
A composed metric should be compared with ground truth. For temporal aggregation the ground truth is the metric measured over the desired interval. For spatial aggregation it is the metric measured on actual traffic rather than on the active sampling streams. Composition can deviate from it because errors in the underlying measurements propagate, and because the measured sub-paths are not identical in scope to the complete path. A metric description MUST include a section identifying the deviation.

If a sub-path cannot be measured during an interval, the result SHOULD be recorded as undefined. Time variation also matters: traffic often varies over the day, and aggregating hourly results into a daily one hides that variation. Metrics that are mostly time-invariant, such as the minimum one-way delay of a stable path, are less affected.
sections.eli5: When you guess the whole trip from its pieces, you should say how far off the guess might be. If a piece was never timed, you write down that it is unknown rather than making up a number.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of any active measurement of live networks apply, and the RFC points to the OWAMP and TWAMP specifications (RFC 4656 and RFC 5357).

Exchanging sub-path measurements between network providers may be a concern. The data should be anonymized enough to avoid revealing unnecessary operational details, such as the network addresses of measurement devices. The schema for such exchange is out of scope and is expected to be covered by bilateral agreements.
sections.eli5: If neighbouring companies share their timing notes, they should hide details like exactly which machines they used.

items.title: Temporal aggregation
items.text: Same metric and scope, different time windows, such as 12 five-minute maxima giving a 60-minute maximum.

items.title: Spatial aggregation
items.text: Same metric type, different scope, possibly weighted by traffic load.

items.title: Spatial composition
items.text: Adjacent sub-paths joined end to end; all sub-paths contribute equally.
